source_contract.full_node_key: canvas-ui.mjs267 serializes the whole normalized node, including absolute rect x/y, as nodeKey for composition detection and GPU text content.
source_contract.raster_key: ui-gpu.js184 includes that full nodeKey plus relative x-x0/y-y0, size, crop dimensions, viewport H and scale.
source_contract.paint: ui-gpu.js89–91 sets scratch transform to(-x0,-y0). canvas-ui.mjs198–201 passes explicit pixel bounds to text painters; styled text/layout uses those bounds and paint properties, not node.rect.
source_contract.confirmed_conditional_redundancy: For the same text/paint properties translated by exact integer framebuffer pixels with unchanged local geometry, crop extent, subpixel phase, viewport and scale, the scratch-local paint is unchanged while full-node absolute x/y changes request.content and forces another raster/upload.
source_contract.constraints: Fractional subpixel movement, crop/clip changes, dimensions, viewport/scale, fonts/styles, text-edit selection/caret/composition and shadow bounds can change pixels and must remain in content identity. GPU quad placement/order/clipping must still update independently.
source_contract.scope: Source-level conditional equivalence, not actual pixel/GPU proof or authorization to modify the renderer.

ui_gpu_raster_audit.observed_conclusion: The cumulative sample shows470rasters/uploads across540submits, with no compaction and31–32live text slots. This is not evidence of re-rasterizing every text node on every frame. It does not isolate which label changed or prove the conditional key redundancy dominates the large ui_draw tail. Rebuild CPU metrics are often under1ms while the aggregate ui_draw tail is much larger, so work before/around GPU rebuild remains unisolated.
